title: Comparison: TRAI vs RBI vs SEBI

blocks.content: Regulatory bodies such as RBI, SEBI, and TRAI serve as autonomous pillars ensuring financial stability, investor protection, and fair market competition across key sectors of the Indian economy.

rows: Securities and Exchange Board of India Act, 1992
Telecom Regulatory Authority of India Act, 1997
Price stability, credit regulation & bank supervision
Fixing tariffs, ensuring fair competition & service quality
Finance Bench / High Courts / Supreme Court

items: RBI was established on April 1, 1935 based on the recommendations of the Hilton Young Commission.
SEBI was non-statutory when formed in 1988 and gained statutory powers via the SEBI Act in 1992.
TDSAT (Telecom Disputes Settlement and Appellate Tribunal) was created by an amendment in 2000 to divest TRAI of its adjudicatory powers.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: RBI functions as the central bank regulating monetary policy, currency issuance, and the banking system under the RBI Act, 1934.
SEBI regulates the securities, capital, and commodities markets to safeguard investor interests under the SEBI Act, 1992.
TRAI regulates telecommunication services, tariffs, and service standards under the Telecom Regulatory Authority of India Act, 1997.
While RBI and SEBI govern core financial sectors, TRAI manages communication infrastructure and tariff fairness.
Adjudicatory functions for TRAI were transferred to TDSAT in 2000, whereas SEBI decisions are appealed before SAT.
